## Hypothesis

The parent's losses are almost entirely on **TPOT** (ratios 1.09, 1.23, 1.20, 1.29, 1.28) while TTFT/E2E sit at par — and its reward contains *no TPOT term at all*. Worse, its reward `1 - lat/target` saturates at both ends: mean reward ≈ 0.90 in the easy episodes (where P99 TTFT is already 7 s, i.e. the tail is invisible inside a saturated reward) and pinned at exactly **-1.0** in the overload/mix episodes (673 s and 1427 s P99 TTFT produce the identical reward as 80 s, so the regime that decides P99 carries zero gradient). With no gradient at the tail and no decode signal, the only consistent training signal left is the DQfD margin loss, and teacher agreement duly climbs to **0.83** — the parent is an expensive copy of the evolved router, inheriting precisely its known defect (TTFT won by packing prefix-sharing sessions, decode batches grow, TPOT 1.04–1.23x). So: the reward must be **scale-free and non-saturating in log-latency** (matching the fitness, which is a *log* P99 ratio), must **price TPOT with the same weight as TTFT**, and the teacher must be **decayed to zero** so the policy is forced off the packing behaviour. The credit path for "my prefill slowed someone else's decode" cannot come from the decision's own outcome, so I add an interval cost with a convex decode-concentration term (plus a convex worst-replica prefill-backlog term), which charges a decision through the bootstrap for the congestion it leaves behind. Features gain the ingredients the evolved router hand-sets as constants: the uncached-work × resident-decode interaction (the per-replica miss surcharge), uncached-work × congestion (miss price rising with load), and in-flight credit for a session's previous turn still queued.

## Hypothesis

The scored loss is 77 % TPOT: the per-scenario log-ratio sum is +1.056 for TPOT versus +0.247 for TTFT and +0.067 for E2E. Under `bandit` credit, a decision's reward contains only *its own* request's outcome, so the one thing routing actually does to TPOT — dropping uncached prefill work on top of decodes that are *already resident* on that replica — is never credited to the action that caused it. The parent substituted a hand-set deterministic price for that externality (`W_INTF`, `W_DEC`, `W_KVP` constants), i.e. exactly the fixed-constant simplification that is supposed to be learned, and it is mis-scaled everywhere at once (TPOT 1.04→1.31x, worst on the ramp). Second, the parent's baseline was keyed on the *endogenous* cluster backlog, so when the policy drove the cluster into deep backlog the baseline followed it and the reward went to ~0 (training reward mean actually *rose* to +0.11/+0.19 in the two mix episodes while P99 TTFT was 260 s / 433 s) — congestion the policy itself created was free.

So: (1) replace the hand-priced decode externality with a **measured** one — when a request completes, charge it the (log) TPOT excess of the requests that were already resident on its replica when it was routed and that finished during its stay; this is real cross-request credit without a bootstrap, with more samples per decision than own-TPOT, and it adapts per trace/regime instead of being a constant; (2) re-key the baseline on **exogenous** conditions only (arrival token rate, prompt size) and blend in a non-adaptive anchored component, so collapse always costs; (3) keep the deterministic miss price at half weight as a prior and add the three decode/outstanding balance terms the net needs to express "pack for prefix, but not onto the decode-heaviest replica". Nothing reward-derived enters the features, since `reward()` is not exercised at scoring.

**Hypothesis.** The parent lost on exactly one axis: TPOT (ratios 1.09–1.29 on five of six scenarios, while TTFT/E2E sat at parity). Its reward contains no TPOT term at all, and both of its terms are *clamped* soft deadlines — `max(-1, 1 - l/target)` — so in the easy regime the reward sits pinned near +0.9 (diagnostics: mean 0.90, first/last 0.875/0.893) and in the regime that actually decides P99 it is pinned at the −1 floor (mix episodes: reward mean −0.46 and −0.82, last = −1.0 exactly). The only regimes with gradient are the uninteresting middle ones. With no signal left to learn from, the margin loss and a never-decaying teacher (`teacher_acted ≈ 0.30` in all 12 episodes, agreement climbing 0.66 → 0.83) made the policy an imitation of the evolved router, inheriting its known defect: it packs prefix-sharing sessions, grows decode batches, and pays for TTFT with TPOT. The upward Q drift (0.58 → 19.4) confirms the targets were a nearly constant positive baseline rather than a discriminative quantity.

So I test: *make the credit non-saturating and in the objective's own currency (log-latency), give TPOT its own channel both retrospectively (the request's own per-token time) and prospectively (an interval cost on the decode imbalance a decision creates, which is the controllable part of ∑ batch², with the exogenous level removed so the bootstrap is not swamped by common-mode noise), and force the teacher out to zero by 25k decisions while exploration is still alive.* Hinges at the tail of each log term add slope precisely in the P99 region instead of removing it. Features add what the policy needs to *price* that trade-off by regime rather than with a constant: decode occupancy and its excess, the cache-miss × resident-decodes surcharge, the cache-miss × global-load interaction, in-flight session credit, and cluster-level load/knee indicators.

**Hypothesis.** The parent's reward is both *level-dominated* and *saturating*, and it has no channel at all for the externality a decision imposes on others. Level: its reward mean slides -0.47 → -5.0 across episodes while across-replica differences stay ~0.1, so the regression spends its capacity on a state value (Q drifts -0.6 → -3.0 in lockstep with congestion) and the argmax over replicas is decided by extrapolation noise — visible as the action-share collapse to 0.18/0.22/0.20 on three replicas precisely in the two mix episodes whose training P99 TTFT explodes to 234 s / 418 s, and as the scored 3.37x TTFT at the Tool knee. Saturation: d(-log1p(ttft))/d(ttft) = 1/(1+ttft) ≈ 0.016 s⁻¹ at 60 s, so in exactly the regime that sets P99 every action earns the same reward. And a per-request reward can never see that a request's TPOT is caused by *later* decisions, which is why TPOT stays 1.05-1.09x in every lineage. So: (1) regress a **centred, convex-in-excess** deviation from an online baseline keyed by (congestion × prompt size) at routing — the level is removed in every regime and the gradient *grows* at the tail instead of vanishing; (2) restore temporal credit with `interval_reward`, but charge the **deviation of the cluster's queueing/decode-excess cost from its own regime norm (keyed by the exogenous offered token rate)** rather than the absolute in-system count — that is what destroyed the earlier DQN, because a discounted action-independent level swamps the advantage; and (3) make the hand-set externality price a *decaying prior* (weight 1.0 → 0.15 over training) so the final policy must rely on the learned bootstrap, not on the constant.

proposer.rationale:
**Hypothesis.** The deficit of this lineage is almost entirely TPOT (log-ratio sum 1.056 vs 0.247 for TTFT, uniform across all six scenarios), and I think the cause is *reward magnitude*, not reward structure. In the parent, `log1p(ttft/1s)` moves over ~0–4 and its per-bucket deviations are ±1–2, so `g()` returns 1–6; `log(tpot/40ms)` deviations are ±0.2–0.4, so `g()` returns ~0.2–0.4. Despite `W_TPOT=1.10 > W_TTFT=1.00`, the squared-error regression therefore spends essentially all of its capacity on the TTFT component and treats TPOT as residual noise — which is exactly what the diagnostics show (TTFT at or below the best heuristic, TPOT 1.04–1.31x everywhere, worst where backlogs are deepest). Inspiration 2 attacked the same symptom through credit, but it injected the *raw summed* resident-TPOT excess into individual rewards (up to 3.5, driven by how many residents happened to complete): that is an action-correlated **level**, the same failure mode as the dqn bootstrap, and it did not help (-0.1695).

Two changes test this. (1) Each reward term is divided by an online estimate of its own dispersion (count-warmed EWMA of |deviation| per exogenous bucket, with a floor), so TTFT, E2E and TPOT contribute comparable gradient energy and the weights finally mean what they say. (2) The measured decode externality is kept but demoted to a *calibration* role: residents' excess TPOT updates a small table keyed by (cluster congestion × candidate decode occupancy × uncached fraction), and what enters the reward is that table's value **zero-meaned across the replicas of the decision** — a low-variance direction with no level, blended out of a hand-set prior as counts accumulate. The hand-set decode/interference constants are removed; their magnitude is now measured per trace and per regime.

proposer.rationale:
## Hypothesis

The parent's regression is healthy (loss 0.31→0.07, uniform action shares, teacher agreement decaying to 0.24–0.52), yet its TTFT win collapsed to parity (0.945–1.206) while TPOT stayed 1.04–1.31x — i.e. it moved to a *worse* point on the frontier than its own ancestors (TTFT 0.51–0.86 / TPOT 1.13–1.23, stage-1 +0.127). The cause I suspect is the **fully-centred reward**: every latency term was replaced by its deviation from an online baseline keyed by (cluster-backlog bucket × prompt size). That baseline tracks the regime, so during a load-ramp peak, a burst pile-up or a mixed workload — exactly the regimes that produce the scored P99 and the worst-scenario half-penalty — a 60 s TTFT is "normal for this bucket" and earns ~0 reward. The design therefore deleted all *absolute* tail pressure precisely where the tail is made, and (because the objective is a log-ratio) traded away the cheap, large TTFT win for nothing: 0.33·log(1/0.6)=0.17 of win is worth three times the 0.33·log(1.2)=0.06 of TPOT loss it was buying. The centring is sound as a variance reducer for the across-replica advantage, but it must not be the *only* channel. Under "bandit" there is no bootstrap to amplify an action-independent level, so an absolute level is harmless to the argmax and merely has to be fitted from the (shared) cluster features.

Change under test (reward only; features and CONFIG topology held fixed to isolate it): each latency term becomes **absolute non-saturating convex penalty + centred convex deviation**, with TTFT weighted above TPOT in proportion to their log-ratio value, TPOT priced as an explicit excess over a target rather than a centred log, and `reward_clip` raised 6→12 so the knee-regime levels are no longer clipped away.

**Hypothesis.** Every reward channel in this lineage is attributed to the *routed* request's own outcome, so a decision is never charged for the congestion it imposes on the requests that come after it — exactly the credit the brief says decides P99 TPOT ("a request's TPOT is caused by LATER routing decisions"). The best ancestor papers over that with a *hand-priced* zero-mean externality (`W_MISS/W_INTF/W_KVP/W_DEC`): constants that encode "a miss costs more where decodes are resident", i.e. precisely the kind of fixed trade-off that is tuned for one regime and breaks on the worst scenario (which fitness penalises at half weight). My hypothesis is that the externality should be *measured on realised state* instead of predicted by constants: charge each decision, one step later, the deviation of the replica it actually chose from the cluster mean congestion *as it turned out* at the next decision — so the price of landing work somewhere is set by how fast that replica really drained in this regime, not by a constant. I therefore add `interval_reward` (one-step credit under the bandit, zero-level by construction since it is a cross-replica deviation), identify the executed action by diffing the replica views against a snapshot taken at the previous decision (returning 0 whenever the identification is not unambiguous, so the design degrades gracefully to its parent), and linearly decay the hand-set price to 35 % of its initial weight over the first 25k decisions so it acts only as an early prior while the measured channel takes over. Everything that worked — bandit regression on a bucket-centred advantage, de-saturated features, teacher phase-out — is kept.

## Hypothesis

The parent's DQN never actually learned a value *ranking* — it learned a drifting level and then filled the vacuum with the teacher. With `beta = 0.05` and ~0.06–0.12 s between routing decisions, the discount per step is ≈0.996: an effective horizon of several hundred decisions, far longer than the causal reach of one routing choice. The diagnostics show exactly that signature: Q climbs monotonically 0.58 → 19.4 and is still climbing after 20k gradient steps (its fixed point with mean reward ≈0.9 is ≈225), so the Huber loss is spent chasing a large *action-independent* value level while the action-dependent advantage is a tiny residual in the noise. With no usable TD ranking, the DQfD margin term dominated (agreement 0.83, teacher share flat at 0.30 because no `*_end` decay was set) and the policy converged to the evolved router — hence it reproduces the teacher's exact defect profile: TTFT/E2E ≈ parity, TPOT 1.09–1.29x, which *is* the evolved router's known 1.04–1.23x TPOT penalty against the per-metric best baseline. The fix tests one thing: make the credit horizon match the physics and remove the level from the target. Concretely (i) `beta = 0.30` (≈3 s horizon, the span over which a prefill chunk actually steals decode steps), (ii) rewards centred on a slow *exogenous* baseline and bounded so |r| ≲ 1 and Q stays O(10) and converges, (iii) the decode externality delivered as **potential-difference shaping** in `interval_reward` (Ng-Harada form, policy-invariant, zero net return) so the harm of adding uncached prefill to the decode-heaviest replica is charged *immediately* instead of having to propagate through a bootstrap chain that the parent's horizon could not support, and (iv) the teacher decayed to near zero with exploration held at 0.05, so two-thirds of training is spent learning where it is wrong.

## Hypothesis

Two things in the parent conspire to produce exactly the scorecard we see — TTFT at or below the best heuristic on steady scenarios but TPOT 1.25–1.32x everywhere and TTFT 1.12–1.15x on the burst/ramp stress cases.

1. **The baseline is endogenous, so congestion is self-excusing.** `_center` keys its online baseline on `lg_mean_pend`, a quantity the policy itself creates. A decision that piles backlog onto the cluster moves the whole population into a higher-backlog bucket, whose baseline then rises to meet it, and the centred reward returns to ≈0. The training logs show the consequence directly: in the two mixed-workload episodes the action share collapses onto one replica (0.28, 0.22) and training P99 TTFT reaches 292 s / 434 s while reward mean *improves* to −0.07. There is no reward gradient that says "this regime is catastrophic", so the learner never learns to refuse to pile on, and that is precisely the burst/ramp deficit.
2. **TPOT credit is attached to the wrong decision and the measured externality is probably inert.** A request's TPOT is caused by *later* arrivals on its replica, so regressing it on the request's own action is mostly noise; meanwhile the "measured externality" is recovered by diffing replica views, which silently returns 0 whenever the diff is ambiguous, and even when it fires it is weighted 0.30 with a ±2 clip against a ±6 own-latency reward. The decode-concentration channel therefore carries almost no weight — hence a chronic TPOT deficit despite `W_TPOT = 1.0`.

The fix tests both with one mechanism each. The relative baseline bucket becomes **exogenous** (long-EWMA offered token rate, prompt size, arrival-rate trend — things the router cannot manipulate) and gains a small anchored absolute term, so catastrophic latency can never be explained away. And the externality is **attributed with certainty at completion time**, where `outcome.replica` is known: I keep a timestamped history of per-replica decode occupancy and pre

## Hypothesis

The parent's loss is almost entirely TPOT: decomposing its fitness (mean of per-scenario `-0.33·Σ log ratio` plus half the worst) gives Conv-ramp as the worst scenario, where TPOT contributes 0.217 of its 0.312 log-loss, and TPOT is ≥1.14 in all four heavy scenarios while TTFT is already ≤1.12. The cause is visible in the reward's *units*, not in the state: TTFT is priced as `0.55·(l+0.15l²)` with `l = log1p(ttft/1.5)`, which at the scored knee (ttft≈20 s, l≈2.7) has gradient ≈1.0 per unit **log-TTFT**, whereas TPOT is priced as excess over target, `0.5·(u+0.3u²)` with `u = tpot/42ms−1`, giving gradient ≈0.27 per unit **log-TPOT** at tpot≈80 ms. The objective weights the two log-ratios equally (0.33/0.33), so the parent's reward is tilted ~4:1 towards TTFT and it correctly bought 0.08 of log-TTFT with 0.18 of log-TPOT — a trade the harness scores as a loss. Second, the only credit for the TPOT *externality* (a decision inflating the decode batch of requests already resident — "a request's TPOT is caused by LATER routing decisions") was a hand-set deterministic surcharge on running-count deviation; the request's own TPOT carries that signal only with a long lag.

So: (1) re-price TPOT in the same log units as TTFT, with gradient ~1.5× TTFT's at the knee (tilted, because TPOT dominates the worst-scenario penalty) and cap the TTFT level so catastrophic mixed-workload episodes cannot drown the decode channel; (2) add a measured `interval_reward` — a Bradtke–Duff charge over the dt to the next decision whose decode channel (mean and max-vs-mean convex batch occupancy) is weighted at least as heavily as the queue channel, so each decision pays immediately for the decode concentration it leaves behind instead of waiting for a lagged own-TPOT; (3) give the network the *future* decode batch (outstanding-request deviation/rank, not just current `running`), since the request it routes joins the batch together with everything already queued there.

## Hypothesis

The parent's residual loss is almost entirely TPOT (sum of log ratios ≈ 1.07 of ~1.29 total), and it is *uniform* across traces and worst at the knee, under bursts and ramps — exactly where the policy packs sessions and grows one replica's decode batch. The reason is **credit, not features**: with `algorithm="bandit"` the only multi-request channel is a single-step `interval_reward`, and that single step (dt ≈ tens of ms) carries almost no weight, while the main target is the request's *own* latency. But a request's TPOT is produced by *later* decisions on the same replica, and P99 is a **max over replicas**, not a mean — so the quantity a decision should be charged for is the *future concentration* of work it creates, integrated over the seconds it persists. A bandit cannot see that; the parent therefore tried to fake it with a snapshot-diffed one-step charge (zero whenever the action diff is ambiguous), which is why TTFT improved slightly but TPOT did not move at all.

So: switch to the **semi-MDP Double DQN** and make the dominant signal a Bradtke–Duff interval cost whose integrand is **cross-replica concentration** of prefill backlog, decode occupancy and KV risk (plus a log-compressed level term, which is the only part the router can move via cache hits). The router cannot change the total offered work, only its distribution, so dispersion is the action-relevant cost — and because it is a `max − mean`, the regime level that poisoned the earlier DQN attempt barely enters the target, while the discount `exp(-beta·dt)` with beta = 0.04 (≈25 s horizon) carries the charge back to the decision that caused it. The request's own TPOT/E2E terms are demoted to shaping (they are mostly caused by other decisions), own TTFT keeps full weight (it *is* this decision's queue), and all baselines are exogenous with a non-adaptive anchor so a collapsing episode can never explain its congestion away. The parent's diagnostics show a policy that is *good at what it is paid for and blind to what it is not*: TTFT 0.92/0.94 at speed 1.0, but TPOT 1.04→1.32 and a growing TTFT loss exactly in the hard regimes (Tool-0.75 burst 1.15, ramp 1.12), with action shares drifting to 2.5x imbalance (0.195 vs 0.076) in the knee episodes. Two credit defects explain this jointly. ## Hypothesis

The parent's reward is a **saturating** soft deadline (`_soft` clips at the target), so at the knee — exactly where P99 is decided — every candidate replica yields the same floor reward and TD/regression carries no ranking signal; Q rose monotonically 0.58 → 19.4 (an action-independent level, horizon ~250 decisions at beta=0.05) while the only consistently-signed gradient left was the DQfD margin term with a teacher share pinned at 0.30 (no `*_end` decay). The bandit-advantage sibling (-0.1387) fixed the saturation but still cannot improve TPOT, because (a) it centres the TPOT baseline on a bucket keyed by **mean pending backlog** — an endogenous quantity, so congestion the policy itself creates raises its own baseline and forgives it, and (b) a request's TPOT is largely caused by *later* decisions, which no per-request reward attributes to the decision that chose the replica.

So the test: keep the bandit (the only credit scheme in this lineage that reached ≈-0.14), but (1) make the centring buckets purely **exogenous** (long-EMA offered token rate × prompt size), (2) price TPOT mostly against an **absolute** per-token reference (0.025 s) with a convex, never-saturating penalty, so decode crowding can never be normalised away, and (3) replace the hand-priced externality with a **measured, correctly-attributed** one: a coarse 0.1 s snapshot ring of per-replica decode-batch excess over the cluster mean, integrated over the 4 s after `routed_at` on `outcome.replica`. That charges the decision that put a request on a replica for the decode concentration it joined/created there — including crowding created by subsequent decisions, which is what the TPOT tail is made of — as a cross-replica deviation, hence level-free. Teacher decays to 0.02 / imitation to 0 by 20k decisions, so it is a prior, not the target.

So: **replace both with an exactly-attributed, measured externality.** At completion `outcome.replica` is known, so I can charge the decision with the chosen replica's *realised excess over the cluster mean* — prefill backlog over a fixed 2 s window after routing, and decode occupancy over a fixed 2 s window starting at first token (fixed-length windows, so invisible output length cannot confound it). That is a cross-replica deviation: it is exactly 0 for a balanced cluster at any load, so it carries no regime level and needs no deadline or tuned price; its magnitude comes from the replica's realised drain rate in *this* regime, which is precisely the "linear guess about how queues grow" that fixed rules get wrong. **Hypothesis.** The parent learned a *state value*, not an *advantage*, and then let the imitation loss do the rest. Its reward is strictly positive-offset (mean ≈ +0.9) and `beta=0.05` with sub-second inter-decision gaps makes γ≈1, so the DQN fixed point is a large common level — exactly what the diagnostics show (Q 0.58 → 19.4, monotone, across every episode, while loss stays flat at ~0.4-0.6). When Q≈19 for every replica, the action-dependent part of the target is ~1 % of the regression target and is swamped by the level; the only clean, action-discriminating gradient left is the DQfD margin term, which is why teacher agreement climbs to 0.83 and the policy inherits the teacher's known weakness (TPOT 1.09-1.29x everywhere) while adding nothing. So the test: make every reward channel **zero-mean and non-saturating** (slow baseline + fixed anchor blend, convex above the norm), so Q hovers near zero and the learned quantity *is* the advantage; move the externality that heuristics hand-price — queueing and decode-batch concentration inflicted on *other* requests — out of the per-request return and into `interval_reward` (Bradtke & Duff), so a decision is charged for the crowding it leaves behind through the bootstrap rather than through a hand-set constant; raise `beta` to 0.1 (≈10 s credit horizon, enough for the queue it creates, short enough to keep Q bounded); and phase the teacher out completely by decision 22k so the last ~38k decisions are learned, not copied.

## Hypothesis

The parent's loss is 77 % TPOT (log-ratio sum ≈ 1.07 vs ≈ 0.31 for TTFT), and the deficit is *uniform* across all six scenarios — including the ones where its TTFT beats every heuristic. A uniform, regime-independent deficit is not a regime-sensing or credit-horizon failure; it is a **reward scaling** failure. Fitness weights log-P99 ratios 1/3 each, but inside the reward the TTFT channel has 4–6× the dynamic range of the TPOT channel (`log1p(ttft/1)` deviations are O(1); `log(tpot/0.04)` deviations are O(0.2)), and the convex `g()` widens that further.
